reviews.text: It's excellent in every way. It's trustworthy.

I visited the clinic with a referral letter.

My elderly cat is being treated for a tumor and lymphatic issues.

The doctor provided attentive care, and she is currently showing signs of recovery. I hope she goes into remission.
My cat, who had been suffering daily from urinary stones, recovered remarkably thanks to Dr. Yonezawa, avoided surgery, and is now able to live happily every day. Thank you so much! 🌷 …

This hospital conveys a sense of sincerity, with all staff members genuinely and enthusiastically dedicated to caring for animals. They cured a difficult-to-treat illness that other hospitals couldn't resolve.

My child had been receiving treatment for cancer for several years.

I informed them that I would be seeking a second opinion because I had obtained information about a treatment plan that hadn't been suggested there. Perhaps their pride was hurt, because from the next appointment onwards, the attitude of both the doctor and the resident changed. The doctor clearly hadn't properly reviewed what I had previously told the resident, resulting in a haphazard examination. They didn't even ask about the next appointment, as they usually do. When I asked the resident about the next appointment before paying, I was told "this is the end" without any explanation, and this was communicated through the resident, not the doctor.

I don't know if they disliked me seeking a second opinion, or if they thought my child's condition was so serious that there were no more options, but I felt their response was irresponsible.

My beloved dog was diagnosed with transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder, and I've been visiting him since 2021, more than four years ago.
The doctors here are passionate about both research, which aims to ensure the healthy future of animals, and clinical work, which aims to cure current animal illnesses.
After participating in a clinical trial for a molecular targeted drug, my dog ​​underwent a total cystectomy in June 2022.
I had heard that it was a very difficult surgery, but thanks to the efforts of his doctor, Dr. Shingo Maeda, and the surgeon who performed the surgery, Dr. Yosuke Takahashi, he is now in good health three and a half years after the surgery. (In fact, during a follow-up visit in October 2024, a malignant liposarcoma was discovered in his abdomen, separate from the bladder cancer, and Dr. Yosuke Takahashi also performed surgery to remove the sarcoma. I can't thank him enough!)
In addition, residents here are responsible for interviews, pre-examinations, and administering medications. The staff range from innocent student-like people to experienced doctors, but they are all kind and polite, and I feel at ease. 

The University of Tokyo Animal Medical Center, which has saved my now 13-year-old dog's life not once but twice, is without a doubt the best animal hospital for our family.

My 12-year-old dog was cared for here.
His doctor recommended several hospitals for the surgery, and our center was one of them.
Since it was my first time, I was naturally worried and gathered a lot of information.
Reviews can be helpful, but they can also make you anxious.

I trusted in fate and asked for your help,
and even though there were many young doctors and staff, everyone was so kind to me.
The surgery was completed successfully, but an unexpected incident (unrelated to our center) meant another surgery was required. Your quick response saved my family's life twice.

I am truly grateful.
I would like to take this opportunity to express my gratitude once again.
Thank you very much.

To everyone who is struggling to choose a hospital like us,
Please do not be alarmed by some reviews,
I believe that trusting your family (and your pet) is one option.

This experience has taught me once again that even in the event of unfortunate events, we must always remember to be polite as human beings.

"We'll do our best and leave the rest to fate."
As a family, all we could do was trust in the doctor and pray...

Thank you for your help with my dog's checkup.
Thank you very much.

I'm so grateful for all the blood transfusions my beloved cat received from you. Even though it was your job, you worked late into the night providing such dedicated care. Thanks to you, she was able to live for two more years, and we have so many wonderful memories together. It's almost been two years since she passed away, and I often think of the time when she was receiving transfusions. We were able to do everything we could to treat her, so I have no regrets...🐱 I wonder what my cat thinks...

My beloved cat had liver surgery here about three years ago.

Liver surgery is highly complex, and there are only a limited number of places that can perform it, so we were referred here.

The results were good, and she's now 16 years old and living a healthy life.

My precious family member's life was taken at this hospital. Since that day, my anger and sadness have remained in my heart. When I checked the names of the doctors involved in the surgery, I found out they were Yosuke Takahashi, Akira Kuwashima, and Ito (a trainee). When the surgery was recommended, I expressed concern about whether my cat would be able to withstand the procedure, given his age. The doctor confidently replied, "The blood test results are fine. As an elderly cat, there are some negative numbers, but surgery is the first option for treatment." If that's what he said, I had no choice but to accept it. I was grasping at straws. After the surgery, I was told the approximate date of discharge (there were actually two surgeries performed; the first one was unsuccessful and required a second surgery). When I visited after the surgery, I noticed that my cat's temperature seemed lower than usual, and I told the doctor. If I hadn't mentioned it, I don't think they would have realized the first surgery had failed. Despite the confident recommendation for surgery, my cat died a few days after the procedure. Although he had been ill, he was healthy and calm for his age until the day before he was hospitalized. The day I went to pick up my child from his journey, I said to the doctor, "Was the surgery a failure?" "My child didn't die of old age. He was killed by the surgery." I said so many things, but the doctor simply bowed his head and said, "I'm sorry."
Your apology is worthless. Please give my child back. And I still haven't been charged for the surgery. This convinced me. They can't charge me because they botched the surgery and caused his death.
I will continue to hate him for as long as I live. At the doctors who rest on their laurels, relying on the reputation of the University of Tokyo and lacking any decent skills. At the doctors who didn't even offer a proper apology. I hope my resentment reaches them.

My appointment was at 10:00 AM, I arrived at 9:30 AM, and wasn't called until after 11:00 AM.
I waited about two hours for tests such as X-rays and ultrasounds, and another consultation (explanation).
Although there was a wait, I felt at ease because they were very kind and thorough in their examination.
The reception and examination rooms are on the second floor, and payment is done at the automated payment machine on the first floor.
It was very cute and heartwarming to hear all the different pets being called by their full names.

My beloved dog broke a bone and underwent surgery here. It's a university hospital, so the fees are high, but the explanations are thorough and I feel at ease, so I'm glad I chose them. The receipt will include all the necessary information for pet insurance. Please note that they only accept new patients referred by their family doctor.

I previously performed a porto-venous shunt surgery on my beloved dog. I was very nervous, but the surgery was successful, and he is doing well since being discharged.

Before the surgery, the possibility of a second surgery was suggested, and the risks of surgery (including the risk of death) were explained to me in detail. Given the many risks, I was unsure whether to go ahead with the procedure, but trusting the doctor was the right decision. Perhaps because he was so well-loved during his hospital stay, he didn't mind going to the hospital for follow-up checkups after being discharged. (He's a dog who hates going to his regular doctor...lol)

Compared to humans, I believe animal medicine is still developing. I believe there are areas where a university hospital can contribute to medical care. I had many concerns, but now I believe this was the right choice.

Thank you so much to all the doctors. I know it's a difficult job, but I can't thank you enough for saving my precious family member.
Referred by a family member, and after being monitored for two weeks, she passed away from stomach cancer. …

My dog ​​was introduced to your clinic and we received excellent care.

Thank you to all the doctors and staff for being so kind and attentive.

I paid 300,000 yen for tests, only to find out nothing. When my pet's condition worsened and I tried to make an appointment for a follow-up, I was told there was nothing they could do. Ultimately, I think they only see animals as research subjects. I'm filled with resentment.
